cards.summary: A pipeline runs stages in order

prompt.text: A CI pipeline usually runs install, lint, test and

answer.text: A CI pipeline usually runs install, lint, test and build before an artifact is deployed.

cards.fullLine: A CI pipeline usually runs install, lint, test and build before an artifact is deployed.

teaching.text: Stages run cheapest and fastest first, so a typo fails in seconds. The build step produces the artifact that later stages promote unchanged.

teaching.alt: A CI/CD pipeline moving from checkout through test and build to staging and production

cards.summary: A workflow is a YAML file on events

prompt.text: In GitHub Actions, what is a workflow?

answer.text: A YAML file that runs jobs on events.

options: A YAML file that runs jobs on events
correct: A YAML file that runs jobs on events

teaching.text: A workflow has a trigger, jobs and steps. Jobs run on runners; steps call actions or shell commands. Reusable workflows and actions keep repetition down.

teaching.search: How to build a complete CI pipeline with GitHub actions
teaching.alt: A walkthrough of building a complete continuous integration pipeline with GitHub Actions

cards.summary: Build once and promote the artifact

prompt.text: the same artifact to every environment.

answer.text: Build the artifact once and deploy the same artifact to every environment.

cards.fullLine: Build the artifact once and deploy the same artifact to every environment.

teaching.text: Rebuilding per environment means the tested bytes are not the shipped bytes. Promote one immutable artifact and let configuration change between environments.

teaching.alt: Rows of servers in a data centre with blue status lights

prompt.text: What triggers a GitHub Actions workflow?

answer.text: An event such as a push or pull request.

options: An event such as a push or pull request
correct: An event such as a push or pull request

teaching.text: Common triggers are push, pull_request, schedule and workflow_dispatch. Choosing the trigger decides how fast feedback arrives and how often the pipeline runs.

teaching.alt: A short hands-on demonstration of a GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow

cards.summary: Many fast tests, few slow ones

prompt.text: The test pyramid puts many fast unit tests at the bottom and few end-to-end tests at the

answer.text: The test pyramid puts many fast unit tests at the bottom and few end-to-end tests at the top.

cards.fullLine: The test pyramid puts many fast unit tests at the bottom and few end-to-end tests at the top.

teaching.text: Unit tests give fast, precise feedback. End-to-end tests prove the whole path but are slow and flaky, so use them for the few journeys that must not break.

prompt.text: Why should a build artifact be immutable?

answer.text: So every environment runs exactly what was tested.

options: So every environment runs exactly what was tested
So it can be edited by hand
So it never needs a version
correct: So every environment runs exactly what was tested

hints: The tested bytes must be the shipped bytes.

teaching.text: An artifact is identified by a version or digest and never overwritten. If something must change, build a new artifact; that keeps the audit trail honest.

cards.summary: CI secrets are injected, not committed

prompt.text: CI secrets must be injected at run time, never committed to the

answer.text: CI secrets must be injected at run time, never committed to the repository.

cards.fullLine: CI secrets must be injected at run time, never committed to the repository.

teaching.text: Store secrets in the CI secret store, scope them to the environment that needs them and mask them in logs. Rotate any secret that was ever committed.

cards.summary: A canary gets a small share first

prompt.text: A canary release sends a small share of

answer.text: A canary release sends a small share of traffic to the new version first.

cards.fullLine: A canary release sends a small share of traffic to the new version first.

teaching.text: The canary proves the new version on a few real requests. Watch error rate and latency against the old version, then widen or roll back.

teaching.alt: Most traffic going to the stable version while a small share goes to a canary

prompt.text: Which is a progressive delivery technique?

teaching.text: Progressive delivery releases to a subset first and widens as confidence grows. Canary, blue-green and ring deployments are all ways to limit the blast radius.

teaching.search: Progressive Delivery Explained Big Bang Blue-Green Rolling Updates Canaries
teaching.alt: An explanation of progressive delivery techniques including blue-green and canary releases

prompt.text: What does testing in production require?

answer.text: Strong observability and a fast rollback.

options: Strong observability and a fast rollback
correct: Strong observability and a fast rollback

hints: You must see the problem and undo it quickly.

teaching.text: Some failures only appear with real traffic. Testing in production is safe only when you can measure the effect, limit who sees it and roll back within minutes.

teaching.alt: An explanation of testing in production with canary deployments and progressive delivery
